title: What's New in AL: Dependency Publishing (2024 release wave 2)

chapters.title: How VS Code handles deployment and failures

features.name: Dependency Publishing
features.description: A feature that automatically detects changes in dependent apps and recompiles direct dependencies during deployment. When publishing changes to an app with dependencies, the system attempts to reapply dependent extensions in the correct order.
caveats: Does not support app downgrades due to potential destructive changes
Requires version compatibility - small changes without version bumps work best
May still fail if there are deep dependency chains not in the workspace

features.name: Dependency Publishing Options - Default
features.description: The default setting recompiles all direct dependencies of a changed app regardless of whether they are in the current workspace. Failed deployments are restored to their original state.
caveats: May fail if indirect dependencies have incompatible changes

features.name: Dependency Publishing Options - Ignore
features.description: The ignore option only recompiles the published app itself without checking dependencies. This can lead to runtime errors for all dependent extensions.
caveats: Causes runtime errors for dependent extensions

features.name: Dependency Publishing Options - Strict
features.description: The strict option requires all dependencies of a changed app to be present in the workspace. It will fail immediately if any dependencies are missing.
caveats: Fails if any direct or indirect dependencies are not in the workspace
Requires including all dependent apps to succeed

features.name: Extension restore on failed deployment
features.description: When a deployment fails during dependency publishing, the original extensions are automatically restored to their previous state, allowing developers to recover without manual intervention.
caveats: Does not work if app version was changed as part of the deployment
Limited to restoring to compatible previous states
